candidates.title: Is this Quebec-developed fruit the 'apple of the future'?
candidates.description: Quebec apple producers say it’s been a good season, harvest- and sales-wise. They say it has much to do with U.S. tariffs and new varieties developed in — and for — Quebec.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ontario municipal elections: A look at 7 mayoral races as voters head to the polls
candidates.description: Monday is municipal election day in Ontario, and people across the province will get a chance to pick their next local leaders. Most polling stations will be open from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m., and residents can find information about where to cast their ballots online.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Niagara artist paints 'love letter to Canada' on retired classic airplane in her Wainfleet, Ont., yard
candidates.description: Niagara artist Paula Jane Marie has taken love for all things Canadian to another level with an unusual canvas in her yard in Ontario's Wainfleet township: an airplane featuring her paintings of a moose, loons and, of course, a beaver.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: A ‘reset’ or ‘one and done’? First Nations and first ministers set to hold historic meeting
candidates.description: The Assembly of First Nations national chief says Monday's historic meeting between First Nations and first ministers is a chance to redefine the relationship between First Nations, premiers and the prime minister, even though it will take place under a cloud of skepticism.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: This Nova Scotian just ran his first marathon. He trained for it by eating donairs
candidates.description: David Wadden ran and biked to 59 donair shops in the Halifax area this year to eat donairs and rate them as part of a charity fundraiser. But that wasn't the hard part. After eating the donair, he faced the ungodly task of running or biking back home.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Convicted murderer who attended McGill's faculty of law now back in custody
candidates.description: Jeffrey George Ewert, a convicted murderer who has stirred controversy while attending law courses at McGill University, is back in custody while authorities look more closely at his case.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: From horses to electric cars: Sask. couple sees world transform over 75-year marriage
candidates.description: Helen and Larry Frey of Fort Qu'Appelle, Sask., have not only witnessed growth in their relationship, but growth in the world around them over their three-quarters of a century-long marriage.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Emergency vehicles escort remains of Pte. Shaun Farrell to Prince Albert
candidates.description: An emergency vehicle procession honoured a soldier who died in the Canadian Forces Base Wainwright fire as his remains travelled through Saskatoon on the way home to Prince Albert, Sask., on Saturday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Sask. Crime Stoppers programs pause tip intake due to national data breach
candidates.description: A news release issued jointly from Crime Stoppers agencies in Saskatchewan confirmed the impact of the national leak in Saskatchewan, saying "the stolen data included information that could potentially identify some people who provided tips."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Q&A: Premier Danielle Smith says she doesn’t need Alberta separatists’ support
candidates.description: Alberta Premier Danielle Smith says she has told members of her party to back the province’s referendum results, or leave. In an interview with CBC’s West of Centre, she says she doesn’t need separatists to get re-elected.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Toronto police seeking mother, 22, for allegedly abducting her 3 children
candidates.description: Toronto police are seeking the public’s help in locating three missing children, allegedly abducted by their mother from the Midland Avenue and Eglinton Avenue East area.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 82 days later, no repairs started on washed-out road dividing small Quebec town
candidates.description: Residents in L’Ascension, Que., are still waiting on repairs after August flooding washed away part of their main road. The municipality's mayor blames the delay for repairs on the bureaucracy of different levels of government.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The Marineland belugas keep dying. Was it a mistake to move them?
candidates.description: The deaths of six belugas at Marineland have raised questions about the impact of the transfers on their health and well-being and whether they were fit to travel. But was there ever a better option for the last captive whales and dolphins in Canada?
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why Nova Scotia's AI data centre feels like a surprise reveal
candidates.description: Construction of Nova Scotia's new AI data centre in Point Tupper is well underway, yet so many people were surprised to learn about it. The CBC's Tom Murphy pieces together the timeline.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The RDSP was meant to help disabled Canadians save for the future. Yet many don't know it exists
candidates.description: The Registered Disability Savings Plan was intended to be a financial safety net for people with disabilities and the families who care for them. But it's only reaching about a third of those it was designed to help.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Will the Alberta referendum feed a more polarized immigration debate?
candidates.description: Beside Alberta Premier Danielle Smith's own political future, the most unresolved questions raised by her referendum concern immigration.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Netanyahu 'fighting for his political life' in 1st Israeli vote since Oct. 7. He might still survive
candidates.description: There are few Israeli analysts willing to write off the country's longest-serving prime minister in Tuesday's election, despite the catastrophic impact of the Hamas-led attacks on Oct. 7, 2023.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Israeli military conducts massive West Bank operation, days before Israel election
candidates.description: The Israeli military continued a massive military operation in the occupied West Bank on Sunday, displacing hundreds of Palestinians and placing major restrictions on movement in response to a gun attack that killed two Israeli soldiers and wounded three others in Hebron on Friday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ukraine says its military did not violate Starlink terms, disputing Elon Musk claim
candidates.description: Ukrainian officials have disputed claims by SpaceX CEO Elon Musk that the country's military violated Starlink's terms of service by using the civilian satellite internet network for offensive drone strikes. Serhii Beskrestnov, a defence technology adviser to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said long-standing restrictions on the civilian system in Ukraine made such offensive use impossible.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Venezuela's opposition leader Machado returns after months in exile
candidates.description: Opposition leader and Nobel laureate María Corina Machado reappeared in Venezuela Sunday for the first time since December, about a month before the U.S. military deposed the country's then-President Nicolás Maduro.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada needs concrete results from EU summit this week, former envoy says
candidates.description: Ahead of this week's Canada-European Union summit, Prime Minister Mark Carney said both parties are hammering out a "new, ambitious alliance" after pledging deeper ties with Europe last month.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Tennessee may try to execute Christa Pike again. The state could face legal hurdles
candidates.description: As Christa Pike continues to recover following her botched execution by the state of Tennessee earlier this month, it remains unclear whether another attempt will be made to execute the convicted murderer. But the state could face some constitutional hurdles if it plans to try again, some legal experts say.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'They’re the nicest people': Obama mocks Trump for hitting Canada with tariffs
candidates.description: Former U.S. president Barack Obama slammed the Trump administration's tariff regime on Saturday, noting the absurdity of engaging in a trade war with Canada.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Tens of thousands march in France as protests continue over schools and living costs
candidates.description: Clashes erupted in Paris as a mass march drew to a close Saturday, with more than 400,000 people rallying across France over school funding and soaring living costs in a fresh challenge to President Emmanuel Macron's government.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Musk says he was behind Starlink speed restriction in Ukraine
candidates.description: Elon Musk said on Saturday that his company SpaceX had throttled the Starlink satellite internet service in Ukraine, disrupting operations that the country relies on to defend itself against Russia.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Israelis are leaving the country in record numbers. Could a looming election accelerate the trend?
candidates.description: A record number of Israelis have left the country in recent years, data shows, and experts are raising the alarm ahead of a "watershed" election that they say could add to the trend and put more strain on the country's economy.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why a new round in the U.S.-Iran conflict could be the most devastating yet
candidates.description: As the U.S. midterm elections approach, intelligence analysts warn that the United States and Israel are preparing for a devastating third round of direct military conflict with Iran. Experts caution that the region is locked in a dangerous, open-ended war of attrition.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Black Sea sailors thought a rescue boat was racing toward them. Instead, it was a drone that sank their ship
candidates.description: The Dignity is one of nearly 50 commercial vessels that maritime analysts say have been attacked in the Black Sea in October alone. The strikes are part of an escalating conflict that has brought much of the traffic through the key shipping corridor to a halt and prompted NATO to step up maritime security, including by deploying more patrol boats and radar.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Can millions of people live on the moon? These scientists say yes — but not for very long
candidates.description: Billionaires like Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos are claiming that we can expect big cities with millions of people on the moon, but a new study found that that may not be possible, so don’t start packing just yet.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Carney says 'direct casualties' are result of Ukraine's restricted access to Musk's Starshield
candidates.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney on Friday criticized a decision to restrict Ukraine's access to Elon Musk's military-grade satellite network, saying the move is costing lives.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump tells South Florida rally that U.S. warships could 'do a little stopover' in Cuba, after Iran
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday told a rally for candidates in South Florida that U.S. warships returning from the Middle East could stop over in Cuba on their way back from the Iran war, his latest suggestion of taking an interventionist approach to the nearby country.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Vivek Ramaswamy stands by ad featuring Amy Acton's mother despite bipartisan criticism in Ohio
candidates.description: Biotech billionaire Vivek Ramaswamy embarked on a statewide bus tour across Ohio with fellow Republicans on Friday, even as his gubernatorial campaign's ad featuring the estranged mother of Democratic rival Amy Acton was sowing growing divisions within his party as they fight to maintain political control of the state.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Loblaw CEO apologizes to 2 million shoppers for personal data hack, offers free credit monitoring
candidates.description: The CEO of Canada’s largest grocery retailer is apologizing to about two million shoppers for a data breach earlier this year.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Musk says SpaceX restricted Ukraine's Starlink connection as service restored
candidates.description: The tech billionaire accuses Ukraine of violating its terms of service by using the network for military activity.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Early reports suggest record high turnout in Serbia elections
candidates.description: Serbia is heading to the polls as a student movement attempts to oust longtime populist leader Aleksandar Vučić.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Suspect in deadly Paris suburb shooting sent for psychiatric observation
candidates.description: He will be observed to evaluate whether his "psychiatric health is compatible with pursuing his interrogation", authorities said.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Israel to close West Bank crossings on election day as crackdown escalates
candidates.description: The Israeli Defense Forces announces restrictions on the movement of Palestinian workers in the run-up to Tuesday's election.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Gabon says access to social media restored after eight-month ban
candidates.description: The authorities had justified the ban by saying online content was fuelling conflict, while the opposition had condemned it as an abuse of power.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: El Salvador president says bodies found in Haiti are not those of hostages
candidates.description: Nayib Bukele says bodies delivered to soldiers are "not our men" amid search for Salvadorans abducted last week.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Obama attacks Trump as he campaigns for Democrats ahead of midterm elections
candidates.description: Obama said the election was "the last best chance to at least rein in some of the foolishness of this administration".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: More than 1,300 arrested as clashes follow another day of mass protests across France
candidates.description: Hundreds of thousands took part in demonstrations in France, with protests also taking place in other European countries.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Vanessa Trump says she is cancer-free six months after revealing diagnosis
candidates.description: The ex-wife of Donald Trump Jr, with whom she shares five children, announced in May that she had been diagnosed with breast cancer.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Man arrested after fire at Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat
candidates.description: Some 200 emergency personnel were deployed to fight the blaze at the Nazi dictator's Alpine residence in Germany.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya
candidates.description: She was a close family member of the first victim, a man who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Three released without charge after fatal arson attack in Ireland
candidates.description: Three people - two women and one man - have been released, and one person remains in custody, gardaí say.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Father who killed Oregon school gunman describes anguish over children he couldn't save
candidates.description: Kaylub Giamanco has been hailed as a hero for killing a teenager who fatally shot three children and a teacher.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Student movement takes Serbia's Vučić to the wire in neck-and-neck election
candidates.description: The Student List has emerged from almost two years of anti-corruption protests to form the biggest challenge to Vučić's rule.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: White House lifts tariffs on some Canadian goods as midterm elections loom
candidates.description: From 30 October, tariffs will be eased on some products, including certain machinery, and placed on others, such as carpets.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Two rescued after Nairobi building collapse with five still missing
candidates.description: Police have launched a manhunt for the building's owner and contractor after the multi-storey building collapsed while still under construction.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Who are the candidates in Brazil's presidential election?
candidates.description: Voters in Sunday's election are choosing between two very different candidates, as Americas correspondent Ione Wells reports from Rio de Janeiro.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Who actually controls Ukraine's access to Starlink?
candidates.description: President Zelensky says limits to the technology continue to affect Ukrainian forces, while US officials and Elon Musk offer conflicting accounts of who controls it.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'I cannot teach you integrity': How employee theft is hurting small businesses in Africa
candidates.description: That Girl Boina's post about why she had closed her beauty parlour struck a nerve with other small business owners.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: The bitter row over military service that could shape Israel's future
candidates.description: The ultra-Orthodox community is resisting being drafted into the Israeli army. But will they now bring down the Netanyahu government?
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Why is Ukraine so reliant on Starlink and can Europe plug the gap?
candidates.description: Ukraine needs another satellite internet service, but a decent alternative to Elon Musk's network doesn't exist - yet.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: A shark went astray and captured Korea's heart - will she finally make it back to sea?
candidates.description: More than a million people flocked to Busan to catch a glimpse of the female dusky shark they called Bukangi.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Man killed by falling tree as Storm Boelo batters Scotland
candidates.description: The 60-year-old man was struck by the tree near Castle Douglas as Storm Boelo brought strong winds and heavy rain to Scotland.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: More wet and windy weather to follow stormy weekend
candidates.description: Following the first two named storms of the season, wet and very windy conditions are set to continue into the start of the new week.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm
candidates.description: Scotland editor James Cook finds out what life is like on board a ship in an untapped oil field awaiting its fate.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Amber weather warning as Storm Boelo hits Scotland
candidates.description: The Met Office has issued an amber warning for wind over Scotland from 21:00 until 21:00 on Sunday.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Storm Boelo to bring severe gales and heavy rain into Sunday
candidates.description: An amber weather warning has been issued for much of Scotland, parts of Northern Ireland and northern England, as Storm Boelo approaches.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: The penguins are noisy, the people fantastic - what it takes to be an Antarctic postmaster
candidates.description: George Clarke from Bristol will run the post office at Port Lockroy in Antarctica from October to March.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Seabirds and sewage among UNESCO status challenges
candidates.description: A report marking 10 years of the Isle of Man as a UNESCO Biosphere highlights the scheme's progress.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Israelis have changed. Will they change their leadership?
candidates.description: Israel is holding a general election this week after years of war. For many Israelis, shaken by the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks and years of war, it is the most consequential in decades.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: This College of Magic turns ordinary kids into cool magicians
candidates.description: The students, many from marginalized communities, learn to conjure up candy, do card tricks — and face the world with a confident, creative and resilient mindset.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Soldiers guard center of Milan as thousands of protesters march in cities across Europe
candidates.description: While protests in France have claimed most international attention, large demonstrations also rocked many European cities Saturday from Milan to Rome to Madrid, Lisbon and Tirana.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Protests roil France once again as police seek to quell violence
candidates.description: Hundreds of thousands turned out across France to protest everything from the lack of school funding to economic inequality. Police also were out in force to prevent a repeat of last week's violence.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Why a far-right cabinet minister in Israel has Netanyahu's ear
candidates.description: Israel's most far-right cabinet minister helped dictate hardline policies toward Palestinians in recent years. Benjamin Netanyahu vows to give him a senior position if Netanyahu is reelected next week.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Musk says SpaceX did restrict Starlink, as Ukraine says the tech has been restored
candidates.description: Musk said Ukraine had been violating Starlink's terms by using it for military activity, as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said normal operating speeds have returned.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Gunmen open fire at a church during a funeral in Jordan, killing 7 and wounding 40
candidates.description: Footage broadcast on Jordanian state television showed three gunmen firing shots at a Greek Orthodox church in the city of Karak on Friday.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: European student protests take aim at Serbia's elections
candidates.description: Students have been protesting across Europe. In Serbia, they've selected candidates to run for parliament in Sunday's elections. And they're aiming to end 14 years of government by the populist leader Aleksandar Vucic.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Drinking water supplies dwindle in Yemeni city besieged by Houthi rebels
candidates.description: Taiz, a city in southwestern Yemen, faces a severe water crisis as Houthi rebels backed by Iran tighten their encirclement. The city has struggled with water issues for over a decade, but the situation has worsened in recent weeks.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Netflix lays off 6% of workforce amidst slowing growth
candidates.description: Netflix is regrouping after the release of its latest quarterly earnings this week. Revenue growth at the streaming giant has slowed as the company works to overhaul its programming unit.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Trade tariffs cause whiplash at Port Milwaukee
candidates.description: Sacha Pfeiffer visits Port Milwaukee to see how President Trump's tariffs have affected the flow of goods and impacted the regional economy.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A consultant is going viral for exposing the cringe-worthy DMs bosses send employees
candidates.description: A management consultant is going viral after he started sharing cringe-worthy anonymous DMs employees get from bosses. Like, ones they get on their wedding day and worse.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: What people aged 50 and older need to know about flu shots
candidates.description: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe asks Dr. Ann Falsey of the University of Rochester Medical School about flu shots for people aged 50 and older.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: More dads taking paid family leave for a new baby, sometimes as much as moms are
candidates.description: The U.S. has no national law for paid parental leave. But in states that do, more dads are using the benefit, sometimes more than moms. The change comes as Americans say having kids is unaffordable.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Is your Medicare Advantage plan ending next year? Here's what to know
candidates.description: Medicare open enrollment runs through Dec. 7, and for as many as 5 million seniors, it will be important to log on and pick a new plan.
candidates.author: NPR
